clips.title: Learn AWS IAM in less than 10 minutes
clips.why: An AWS developer advocate explains users, roles and policies in plain words, and why least privilege, giving a job only what it needs, is better than administrator access.
look: The visitor pass: a role gives you credentials for a while, and then they expire. That is what Nova's VM gets.
Policies as permission slips written in JSON: the same Effect, Action and Resource you write in the lab.
Least privilege: give only what the job needs, which for the sandbox VM is a single action.
clips.after: Nova's VM wears a role with one permission slip on it, so even a fooled agent holds a visitor pass to almost nothing.

clips.title: IAM Policy Evaluation Logic | AWS IAM
clips.why: The core rules of evaluation, then a flowchart that walks one request through every kind of policy, SCPs included.
look: The default for every request is deny; an Allow changes that, and an explicit Deny overrides any Allow.
Where SCPs sit in the flowchart: before the role's own policies, so their Deny is final.
A request needs an Allow somewhere and no Deny anywhere. Compare it with the ImplicitlyDenied and ExplicitlyDenied lines in the lab.
clips.after: The ai-agents account's SCPs sit at the top of that flowchart, which is why no role in the account can create a way out of the sandbox network.

clips.title: IAM AssumeRole Basics - 1-minute IAM - Amazon Web Services
clips.why: A short look at assuming a role through STS, and at where you configure who is allowed to assume it.
look: Assuming a role is a call to STS, which answers with temporary credentials.
Who may assume the role is part of the role itself: that is the trust policy.
clips.after: EC2 assumes ai-agent-sandbox for the VM, and the trust policy names only ec2.amazonaws.com, so nothing else can wear that role.

practice.q: Complete the trust policy so that only EC2 machines can wear the sandbox role.
practice.hint: The service name of EC2, followed by amazonaws.com.
practice.why: The Principal of a trust policy says who may assume the role. Naming the EC2 service means only a VM that carries the role through an instance profile can use it.

practice.q: Which Resource lets the sandbox role complete lifecycle actions on ai-agents-sandbox-lite and ai-agents-sandbox-full, but not on a group called fcp-prod-web?

options.why: A bare * matches every group in the account, fcp-prod-web included.
The name must start with ai-agents-sandbox-, so lite, full and wide match and nothing else does.
That matches only the lite group, so a full VM could never tell its pool that it is ready.

practice.q: A program on Nova's VM calls AWS. Put what happens in order.
items: When the VM starts, EC2 attaches the role ai-agent-sandbox through the instance profile
The program fetches temporary credentials from the VM's metadata service
It signs its request to AWS with those credentials
IAM looks for a statement that allows the action and checks for any Deny
AWS runs the call, or answers AccessDenied
practice.why: The role is attached once, at launch. After that, every single request is signed with short-lived credentials and checked on its own.

practice.q: A teammate attaches AdministratorAccess to the sandbox role "just for this week" to test something. What does that change when a poisoned comment fools Nova?

options.text: Nothing, because the VM still has no access key on its disk
options.why: The VM never needed a key on disk. The role's temporary credentials are enough, and now they allow everything.

options.text: A fooled agent can now do anything in the account, such as terminating machines or reading buckets
options.why: We assume the agent can reach root on its VM, and root can use the role. Whatever the role allows, the agent can do.

options.text: Only Nova's own runs are affected, because the role is per run
options.why: The role is shared by every sandbox VM, and its permissions cover the whole account.

practice.q: The sweeper may terminate an instance only if it carries the tag ai-agents:managed=true. Complete the condition key.
practice.hint: aws:ResourceTag/ followed by the tag's key.
practice.why: aws:ResourceTag/<key> is the value of that tag on the thing being acted on, so untagged machines, like the proxy servers, are left alone.

practice.q: What is true about an SCP on the ai-agents account?

options.text: It gives every role in the account a basic set of permissions
options.why: An SCP never grants anything. A role still needs its own Allow.

options.text: It limits what any identity in the account can do, an administrator included
options.why: It sits above the account, nobody inside the account can change it, and its Deny is final.

options.text: It is the trust policy of the whole account
options.why: Trust policies belong to roles. An SCP only limits what can happen inside the account.
